policies.sentence: Students must not use generative AI to produce code, solutions or text for graded work; doing so is cheating.
Students must not submit AI-generated or copied content as their own work; it is plagiarism.
Students must not use AI without instructor permission, attribution or disclosure; such use violates integrity policy.
Instructors and staff pursue suspected AI misuse as academic misconduct or integrity violations through formal channels.
Violating the course AI policy counts as an honor code or academic integrity violation.
Students are accountable for their AI use under the university's academic integrity or dishonesty policy.
Using generative AI for assignments counts as cheating or misconduct under the integrity policy.
Using AI assistants during exams, quizzes or in-class sessions is an integrity violation.
Students must not use generative AI deceptively or maliciously, such as to impersonate people or harass others.
Students must not misrepresent their own engagement, such as inflating hours, having others run AI sessions, or copying session logs.
Submitting the required reflection form and transcript does not excuse a violation of the AI conditions.
Students must not copy or submit others' work as their own; this is academic dishonesty.
Students must cite collaboration and must not share their code after the course ends.
AI chatbots make unauthorized assistance easier and have raised cheating.
Deviating from the AI heuristics does not automatically qualify as academic misconduct.
